description: Pashhur was the priest in charge of the temple, and he had God's prophet arrested and beaten. You can hold a position of spiritual leadership and still not know His voice.
excerpt: We should not assume that just because someone leads in a church, they are close to God. Some are. Some aren't. Position doesn't equal proximity.
verse: "Now Pashhur son of Immer, the priest in charge of the Temple of the Lord, heard what Jeremiah was prophesying."
body_html:
Pashhur was the priest in charge of the temple. That's a big deal. This wasn't a random guy in the crowd. He held a position of spiritual authority, chosen for leadership over God's house.

And yet when he heard Jeremiah prophesying, he didn't recognize it as God's voice. Instead, he had Jeremiah arrested, beaten, and put in stocks overnight.

A priest of God, so far from God that he beat up the actual prophet of God.

This ties directly into the last blog I wrote on Jeremiah 7:22. God had said what He wanted from His people was relationship, not just sacrifices. Pashhur is the picture of what happens when you skip the relationship and keep the ritual. You end up serving in God's house while being deaf to His voice.

You can hold a position of leadership and not know Him.

You can perform every ritual and still miss Him when He shows up.

You can even attack the people He sent because they don't sound like the voice you've grown comfortable with.

The scary part isn't just Pashhur. It's that he was one of many. There were priests all through Jeremiah's ministry who opposed him. Religious leaders who told the people what they wanted to hear while silencing the ones telling them the truth. And they didn't see themselves as the enemy. They thought they were the good ones. They had the robes, the titles, the temple, the position.

We should not assume that just because someone leads in a church, they are close to God. Some are. Some aren't. Position doesn't equal proximity.

Which is why our own relationship with God matters so much. If we're only getting Him secondhand through whoever is leading us, we're in trouble. Because leaders can drift. They can be wrong, they can even attack the ones God is actually speaking through.

The only way to spot a Pashhur is to know God's voice yourself.

Do you know His voice well enough to recognize it, even when someone in leadership is telling you something different?
question: Do you know His voice well enough to recognize it, even when someone in leadership is telling you something different?
